title: Minimax Regret for Monotone Lipschitz Continuous-Dose Policies with Unknown Treatment Density
banked_reason: D0.5 novelty panel: subfield, meets_floor=false, paper_score_ceiling=7.2 < ceiling_for_field=7.4, salvageable=false; math and decision panels pass.
gap_reasons: The contribution remains confined to a three-dimensional uniform covariate design, fixed smoothness radii, and an observed-regression functional rather than deterministic-policy welfare.
The fixed-Lipschitz attaining procedures require exponential exact-net optimization, while the unrestricted construction supplies a statistical rather than practically deployable learner.

These scope and computational limitations, together with the absence of an application demonstrating the value of the new frontier, constrain its leading-journal significance despite the matched minimax statements.

proof_attempt_summary: The run derived exact same-class minimax regret rates for observed response-surface decisions: n^(-1/4) for monotone and ordinary fixed-Lipschitz policies and (log n/n)^(2/11) for unrestricted policies. A causal welfare interpretation failed identification review and was removed; the corrected math and decision panels passed. The novelty panel capped the delivered package at subfield, below the field floor; polynomial-time attainment remains open.
tldr: For individualized continuous doses, exact policy geometry and action localization interact. For the observed response-surface value \(V_P^{\mathrm{obs}}(\pi)=\int\mu_P(x,\pi(x))\,dP_X(x)\), the full interacting coordinatewise nonincreasing class with fixed Euclidean Lipschitz radius has exact minimax expected regret \(\Theta(n^{-1/4})\) under an unknown treatment density. Removing monotonicity leaves this rate unchanged, whereas removing the fixed Lipschitz restriction yields \(\Theta((\log n/n)^{2/11})\). These are observed-law frontiers; the note makes no deterministic-policy causal identification claim.
gap: Existing continuous-treatment policy theory supplies kernel evaluation and sieve oracle inequalities, but no inspected result gives a same-class minimax converse and attaining learner for the full interacting monotone-Lipschitz class under an unknown treatment density.
fill: The project combines exact internal policy nets, endpoint-valid increment smoothing, an integrated orthogonal score, and a graph-localized Assouad family to determine the polynomial frontier and compare monotone, nonmonotone Lipschitz, and unrestricted rules.
